tasks.short: Answer media inquiries and arrange the right spokesperson.

steps.what: Read the media inquiry in the {EMAIL} and record its deadline.
Find relevant facts, previous responses and approved releases in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Inquiry text and permission-filtered documents retrieved from the {DOCS}.
loop.output: Relevant passages with source links, approval dates and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require a supporting passage for each fact; flag expired approvals and conflicting sources.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt across at most 20 passages; unresolved questions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search retrieves documents, but varied questions require reading passages to identify relevant answers.

steps.what: Choose the response approach and spokesperson with the relevant subject matter expert.
Draft a written response and spokesperson briefing in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Response plan, source pack and approved response templates.
loop.output: Response draft and briefing with sentence-level factual references.
loop.check: Check names, numbers and quotations against sources; flag unsupported claims and unanswered questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence or sensitive unresolved questions require manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover acknowledgements, but substantive answers require adapting free text to the question.

steps.what: Review factual accuracy, disclosure limits and the proposed response.
Send the approved response and arrange any interview through the {EMAIL}.
Answer follow-up questions or conduct the interview with the journalist.
Update the media inquiry register and assign outstanding follow-ups in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure an inquiry queue in the {WORKFLOW}, connected to the {EMAIL}, {CALENDAR} and permission-filtered {DOCS}. Bounded extraction and drafting produce sourced response packs; approval binds the exact response, recipient and release time before sending. The queue records correspondence automatically, while people choose spokespersons, handle conversations and confirm follow-ups.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved facts were scattered, source approval dates were unclear, and response handling depended on personal mailbox habits.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queues and scheduling controls handle administration; small extraction and drafting loops can work over a restricted source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Embargoes, hostile questions, conflicting facts and spokesperson availability require judgement. Journalist contact data and confidential briefings require GDPR-compliant processing.
tasks.human_edge: Read the journalist's intent, judge when silence would mislead, and maintain trust during difficult exchanges.

ambition.what: Source-linked briefing packs for specialist journalists.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching and chasing to preparing spokespersons and resolving sensitive inquiries. Formal authority to speak for the organisation does not automatically change.

reach.task: Prepare crisis-response escalation options.
reach.learn: Escalation thresholds, disclosure limits and how to brief an accountable decision maker.

evidence.claim: Archive question answering is being tested; this supports retrieval assistance, not unattended media responses.
A professional-writing experiment included press releases and emails and found productivity gains.
Inquiry routing, version-bound approval and correspondence logging can use configured workflows.

assumptions: Shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates for a mid-size European company.
The queue captures messages automatically; a person confirms deadlines and sensitive classifications.
The sending gate reuses the recorded response approval; edits invalidate that approval.
Access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Which spokespersons can address which subjects?
Where are approved facts, embargoes and disclosure limits recorded?
Can the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR} support shared access and logged sending?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed workflow?
research_questions: How reliably does retrieval distinguish superseded responses from currently approved facts?
Which inquiry categories need specialist legal or financial review?
new_work: Maintain the source approval dates and spokesperson roster.
Review unsupported answers, deadline ambiguities and sensitive inquiries.
Confirm conversation follow-ups and remove contact data under the retention policy.
Maintain connectors, permissions and response templates.
tasks.statement: Respond to requests for information from the media or designate an appropriate spokesperson or information source.

tasks.short: Build cooperative relationships with community, consumer, employee and public interest groups.

steps.what: Review contact history and current concerns before approaching a group.

loop.input: Authorised contact records, meeting notes and concern log entries.
loop.output: Stakeholder brief with dated concerns, commitments and source references.
loop.check: Require source references; distinguish recorded statements from interpretations; specialist checks sensitive context.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per brief; missing or conflicting records go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dates and contacts are structured, but concerns and relationship history are recorded in free text.

steps.what: Exchange availability and arrange a meeting.
Listen to concerns, explain positions and explore common ground.
Write up concerns, proposed commitments and responsible colleagues.

loop.input: Specialist's meeting notes and existing contact record.
loop.output: Proposed record changes and commitments with owners, dates and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Compare changes with notes; never infer agreement, an owner or a deadline; specialist approves changes.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved fields remain blank and enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe concerns and tentative commitments without consistent fields.

steps.what: Approve proposed commitments requiring resources or a change in position.
Send agreed follow-up and set reminders for promised actions.

tasks.design: Configure contact history, commitment fields and reminders in the {CRM}, linked to the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL}. Bounded extraction prepares source-linked briefs and proposed record changes from authorised notes in the {DOCS}; people conduct conversations, approve commitments and review external follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact records could already hold dates and reminders, but scattered notes made useful preparation and accurate follow-up expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Small text-extraction loops can sit inside existing record workflows; AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting fields and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, conflicting interests and informal promises need human interpretation. Sensitive relationship notes need careful access and retention.
tasks.human_edge: Earn trust, notice hesitation and negotiate commitments the organisation can honour.

ambition.what: Regular listening appointments for local community groups without an existing contact.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time reconstructing history and chasing actions, leaving more time for listening. Decision rights remain within the existing relationship and commitment mandate.

reach.task: Arrange accessible community listening sessions.
reach.learn: Accessible invitations, venue requirements and participation formats.

evidence.claim: Contact records, scheduling links, templates and reminders can support relationship administration; relationship quality remains human work.
Extracting tentative commitments from notes needs source checks and human review; this design has no demonstrated relationship outcome.

assumptions: The task covers a typical mix of relationship maintenance and meetings in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
The conversation-heavy prior is retained; administrative work is a minority of total time.
Scheduling automation starts only after the specialist chooses the contact and meeting purpose.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a limited pilot; consultation waiting time may extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Where contact history is stored and whether it can be accessed through supported interfaces.
Which commitments need management approval.
Whether existing notes include sensitive personal data.
Which community groups currently lack regular contact.
research_questions: How often do notes contain ambiguous commitments that cannot be extracted reliably?
Can existing contact and scheduling features cover the pilot without custom code?
new_work: Review extracted concerns and proposed commitments.
Resolve missing owners, dates and conflicting records.
Maintain contact permissions, retention rules and follow-up templates.
tasks.statement: Establish or maintain cooperative relationships with representatives of community, consumer, employee, or public interest groups.

tasks.short: Coordinate production staff and partners to turn approved promotional plans into finished materials.

steps.what: Assemble production requirements from the approved campaign brief in the {DOCS}.
Discuss feasibility, dependencies and creative requirements with production staff.
Agree the production approach, delivery dates and responsibilities.
Enter owners, deadlines and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Chase routine production updates through the {EMAIL}.
Review production proofs against the brief and request corrections.

loop.input: Production proof, production brief, brand guidelines and approved claim register.
loop.output: Draft discrepancy list with proof locations and supporting references.
loop.check: Rules check dimensions, required wording and dates; a person judges message, imagery and claims.
loop.stop: One assessment and one correction pass per proof; unreadable or ambiguous material goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch fixed requirements but cannot reliably compare meaning across varied copy and layouts.

steps.what: Approve final materials and authorize their handoff to the production partner.

tasks.design: A template generator assembles the production brief from approved fields in the {DOCS}, and configured rules in the {PROJECT} create tasks and surface blockers. A bounded proof checker drafts discrepancies against approved requirements; people resolve creative trade-offs and authorize the final partner handoff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived in different document formats. Teams relied on conversations and mailbox follow-up to keep production aligned.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing task rules handle routing and deadlines. AI-assisted coding makes a small template generator and proof-checking connector cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Creative quality, changing specifications and partner capacity remain judgement calls. Reliable checks on complex visual proofs can be expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Translate creative intent into feasible production choices and resolve disagreements without losing the message.

ambition.what: Weekly production risk review across active campaigns

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling packs and chasing updates, and more time resolving production risks. Formal budget and release approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Check artwork readiness before production.
reach.learn: File specifications, accessibility requirements and how layout changes affect meaning.

reach.task: Prioritize production changes across concurrent campaigns.
reach.learn: Capacity planning and the cost of late specification changes.

evidence.claim: Rule-based style checks can support repeatable quality gates; they do not establish creative quality.
Task routing, template assembly and shared status records are established deterministic patterns.
The proposed effort and remaining-time estimates are design assumptions, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: A shared {PROJECT} holds production tasks, while the {EMAIL} still carries follow-up and approvals.
Approved campaign fields and claim references can be maintained in the {DOCS}.
Routine chasing disappears only if production staff update the shared board; exception conversations remain.
Build ranges cover a first usable workflow and can overlap with other tasks.
GDPR applies to personal data. Access review includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Which proof formats, task rules and connectors are available?
Who may approve production changes and partner handoffs?
Do production partners use the shared board?
Which national rules and existing employee agreements apply?
research_questions: Which proof defects can be checked reliably without interpreting imagery?
Does the shared board remove routine chasing during a live campaign pilot?
new_work: Review generated production briefs for missing requirements.
Resolve proof-checker false positives and unreadable files.
Maintain task templates, claim references and connector permissions.
Handle overdue dependencies and partners who do not update shared records.
tasks.statement: Confer with production or support personnel to produce or coordinate production of advertisements or promotions.

tasks.short: Arrange public appearances and events that build awareness and goodwill.

steps.what: Agree event objectives, audience and constraints with the client or public relations manager.
Compare venues and appearance opportunities in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss availability, audience fit and terms with hosts and speakers.
Approve the event budget and proposed terms in the {DOCS}.
Confirm approved bookings and record supplier acknowledgements through the {EMAIL}.
Maintain the event schedule, responsibilities and logistics checklist in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare speaker briefs and the running order in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Confirmed schedule, event objectives and approved organizational facts.
loop.output: Speaker brief with sourced talking points; running order assembled from confirmed timings.
loop.check: Validate timings and names against booking records; specialist checks tone and factual support.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing facts remain explicit questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: The running order is deterministic, but audience-specific talking points need prose adaptation.

steps.what: Coordinate setup, brief hosts and resolve live changes at the venue.

tasks.design: Create event records in the {WORKFLOW}, with rule-based opportunity filters, approved booking fields and a reusable logistics checklist linked to the {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR}. Deterministic templates prepare confirmations, while a bounded loop drafts speaker briefs in the {DOCS}. Exact spending commitments require budget-owner approval; relationship discussions and live coordination stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event software could track dates, but supplier terms, approvals and responsibilities were scattered across conversations and separate files.
tasks.enabler_now: A small records app and existing workflow features can connect those artefacts. A bounded drafting loop handles the variable wording of speaker briefs.
tasks.still_hard: Audience fit, negotiation and live changes remain situational. Unstructured supplier acknowledgements and nonstandard contracts still need manual handling.
tasks.human_edge: Earn cooperation from hosts and speakers, negotiate trade-offs and respond calmly when plans change.

ambition.what: A repeatable community speaker programme for local associations.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time maintaining schedules and more time developing hosts and preparing speakers. Spending and contractual decision rights remain with the budget owner.

reach.task: Build a venue readiness plan and contingency schedule.
reach.learn: Supplier dependencies, accessibility requirements and escalation timing.

reach.task: Evaluate which appearances support a communication objective.
reach.learn: Audience fit, reputational trade-offs and outcome-based evaluation.

evidence.claim: Event records, checklist templates, calendar synchronization and approval-bound confirmations are deterministic workflow patterns.
The MIT writing trial supports bounded assistance with professional prose, but provides no evidence for automating event negotiation.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The people-heavy prior is retained; paperwork can change independently of the conversations.
Shortlist filters use explicit constraints and maintained records; a person assesses audience fit.
Only confirmations matching approved supplier, amount, date and terms can be sent automatically.
Ambiguous acknowledgements and changed terms return to a person.
GDPR applies to contact and attendee data; national rules determine consultation requirements.
The specialist has existing delegated authority for nonbinding discussions and live coordination.
unknowns: Existing event records, approved suppliers and booking channels.
Spending limits and contract-signing authority.
Access to shared calendars and event contact records.
Typical frequency of cancellations and nonstandard terms.
Applicable attendee-data and employee-consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which booking confirmations can use structured fields without losing contractual meaning?
Which readiness checks predict preventable event failures?
new_work: Maintain opportunity records, supplier details and checklist templates.
Review changed terms and unclear supplier acknowledgements.
Resolve calendar synchronization and notification failures.
Review speaker drafts before sharing them.
tasks.statement: Arrange public appearances, lectures, contests, or exhibits for clients to increase product or service awareness or to promote goodwill.

tasks.short: Study organisational goals and stakeholder needs to develop a public relations strategy.

steps.what: Collect organisational goals, policies, previous results and stakeholder evidence.
Clarify priorities, constraints and stakeholder needs with responsible managers.
Draft strategy options with audiences, messages, channels, assumptions and measures.

loop.input: Approved strategy brief, constraints and source-linked evidence bundle.
loop.output: Up to three strategy options with explicit assumptions, evidence gaps and proposed measures.
loop.check: Trace factual claims to sources; validate budgets and dates deterministically; specialist checks feasibility and framing.
loop.stop: Three options maximum and one revision pass; missing evidence becomes an open question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the document, but connecting audience needs, messages and alternatives requires contextual drafting.

steps.what: Choose a recommended strategy and resolve conflicting objectives.
Approve the strategy, resource envelope and escalation boundaries.
Transfer approved milestones, owners and measures into the delivery plan.

tasks.design: A deterministic job assembles authorised objectives, results and stakeholder evidence from the {DOCS}, {BI}, {CRM} and {SOCIAL}. A bounded drafting loop fills structured strategy options, while people choose and approve the direction; approved fields populate the {PROJECT} delivery plan and review schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence assembly and document preparation were fragmented, while strategic choices could not be reduced to fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes modest integrations cheaper to build, and source-constrained drafting can accelerate option preparation without assuming better strategic judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Public opinion is uncertain, attribution is weak and organisational objectives may conflict. A polished option can still rest on a poor assumption.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a credible position, understand stakeholder legitimacy and accept responsibility for strategic trade-offs.

ambition.what: Monthly review of the strategy's highest-risk audience assumption.

tasks.altitude: The specialist shifts time from assembling documents to testing assumptions and defending choices. The specialist can propose more frequent adjustments; the manager retains strategy and resource approval.

reach.task: Align public relations objectives with campaign investment decisions.
reach.learn: Budget trade-offs, outcome measures and the limits of attributing business results to communication.

reach.task: Design a small study to test an audience assumption.
reach.learn: Research questions, sampling and useful evidence thresholds.

evidence.claim: The trial of 444 professionals supports faster preparation of writing tasks, not proof of better public relations strategy.
Coosto supports topic monitoring, providing one possible input to strategy evidence gathering.
Full Fact AI flags checkable claims and matches repeats; claim checks do not establish strategic suitability.
Structured approval fields can populate delivery plans deterministically after approval.

assumptions: This is ordinary organisational public relations, without electoral persuasion.
The high amplification prior supports faster preparation; it does not justify automating strategy selection.
Approved strategy fields contain explicit owners, dates and measures before transfer.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; consultation and employee-data requirements follow applicable national rules.
Build ranges assume a limited pilot using supported interfaces and include active access and consultation work.
unknowns: Whether objectives and promotional policies are current and accessible.
Which outcomes have usable baselines and which are only activity counts.
Who can approve resources and strategy changes.
Whether stakeholder evidence is representative enough for the proposed choices.
Which interfaces and internal approvals are available.
research_questions: Which recurring assumption has the greatest effect on strategy choices?
Can option quality be assessed without rewarding document polish over evidence?
Which delivery-plan fields can existing workflow configuration populate reliably?
new_work: Review option evidence, assumptions and factual claims.
Maintain approved strategy templates and field mappings.
Investigate evidence gaps before committing resources.
Review strategy assumptions against subsequent results.
tasks.statement: Study the objectives, promotional policies, or needs of organizations to develop public relations strategies that will influence public opinion or promote ideas, products, or services.

tasks.short: Discuss stakeholder concerns with managers and advise on business decisions.

steps.what: Gather coverage, stakeholder concerns and relevant business updates.
Prepare a briefing on emerging themes, uncertainties and decisions needing discussion.

loop.input: Dated evidence bundle and previous decision log.
loop.output: Source-linked themes, conflicting accounts and questions for managers.
loop.check: Validate references and dates; show source counts without claiming representativeness; specialist checks framing.
loop.stop: One classification and one correction pass per brief; disputed themes remain flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Stakeholders express similar concerns in different language, and their context matters.

steps.what: Discuss concerns, business constraints and likely public reactions with managers.
Recommend a response and explain reputational trade-offs.
Confirm the business decision and record its owner and review date.

tasks.design: A scheduled job assembles authorised coverage and concern records from the {SOCIAL}, {CRM} and {DOCS}. A bounded classification loop prepares a cited briefing; managers and the specialist discuss its implications, then a configured {PROJECT} workflow records the manager's decision and review date.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was fragmented, and interpreting concerns required manual reading. Existing reporting did not resolve disagreement about business implications.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported exports and inexpensive integration code can assemble evidence; bounded text classification can prepare themes for review.
tasks.still_hard: Coverage is a biased sample of opinion. Advising managers still requires business context, judgement and the confidence to challenge a proposed decision.
tasks.human_edge: Connect public concerns to business choices and challenge assumptions in a difficult management conversation.

ambition.what: Weekly triage of emerging stakeholder concerns.

tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter and more consistent, allowing a weekly concern discussion between larger reviews. The specialist gains a stronger evidence base; managers retain business decision authority.

reach.task: Test whether a prominent concern extends beyond vocal stakeholders.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, survey design and the difference between mentions and prevalence.

evidence.claim: Coosto supports conversation and news-topic monitoring; this supports evidence gathering, not automated business advice.
Deterministic collection and reviewed theme classification are feasible; their value depends on source coverage and managerial use.

assumptions: Most discussion and advice remain human, consistent with the communication-heavy prior.
Coverage sources are licensed or otherwise authorised for the intended processing.
The concern brief describes observed evidence rather than measuring population opinion.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; access and any employee consultation follow applicable national rules.
Build ranges cover a pilot and active consultation work, excluding uncertain waiting periods.
unknowns: Which monitoring sources and business updates are available.
Whether concern records can be linked without exposing unnecessary personal data.
Who owns business decisions and can schedule follow-up reviews.
How often managers currently receive usable concern briefings.
research_questions: Which themes require direct stakeholder research before advice is credible?
What evidence would cause managers to reconsider a recorded decision?
new_work: Review theme framing, source selection and contradictory evidence.
Maintain source connectors and topic definitions.
Check whether scheduled decision reviews occur and capture what changed.
tasks.statement: Confer with other managers to identify trends or key group interests or concerns or to provide advice on business decisions.

tasks.short: Work with agencies and internal staff to agree promotional campaigns, spending and delivery plans.

steps.what: Discuss campaign objectives, audiences and constraints with the marketing manager.
Write the agency brief in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Confirmed objectives, constraints, brand guidelines and approved claim register.
loop.output: Draft campaign brief in a fixed template, with unresolved questions marked.
loop.check: Required-field validation, source references and specialist review of audience and message choices.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing objectives or unsupported claims return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but turning contextual objectives into clear agency instructions needs language synthesis.

steps.what: Send the brief and clarify proposal requirements with the agency.
Compare agency proposals, fees, deliverables and exclusions in a {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: Agency proposals and a fixed comparison schema.
loop.output: Source-linked fee, deliverable, timing and exclusion fields.
loop.check: Code checks totals, currencies and missing fields; the specialist checks scope equivalence.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per proposal; unclear fees or exclusions remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals express scope and exclusions in inconsistent prose, although calculations are deterministic.

steps.what: Negotiate campaign approach, deliverables, timing and commercial trade-offs with the agency.
Approve campaign scope and spending through the {PROCUREMENT}.
Enter approved campaign milestones and production requests in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A brief generator in the {DOCS} combines confirmed campaign fields with a bounded drafting loop, while a proposal extractor fills a comparison table in the {SPREADSHEET}. Existing approval rules in the {PROCUREMENT} control spending, and the approved scope creates milestones in the {PROJECT}; agency negotiation stays with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency proposals used different scope descriptions and fee structures. Decisions depended on relationships and trade-offs that a campaign form could not settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can normalize proposal prose while code checks arithmetic and completeness. Small connectors can reuse existing approval and task features.
tasks.still_hard: Equivalent-looking proposals may buy different rights, quality or reach. Negotiating value and judging channel fit remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether an agency understands the audience and negotiate a workable campaign without weakening its purpose.

ambition.what: Fortnightly channel reallocation review using comparable campaign plans

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week testing campaign choices and negotiating scope, with less brief assembly and proposal copying. Spending and contractual approval rights stay with designated approvers.

reach.task: Recommend changes to channel spending.
reach.learn: Incremental reach, attribution limits and contractual cancellation costs.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Challenge the audience assumptions in an agency proposal.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, audience evidence and how to frame a testable campaign hypothesis.

evidence.claim: A controlled study found productivity and quality gains on professional writing tasks; it did not test agency negotiation.
Repeatable style checks can support review of generated briefs.
Proposal extraction, arithmetic checks and approval routing are a proposed combination, without a documented end-to-end case here.

assumptions: The specialist coordinates agencies but does not independently commit campaign spending.
A {SPREADSHEET} bridges proposal documents because agency scope is not standardized.
The first release covers brief drafting and comparison, not automated media buying.
GDPR applies to audience and contact data; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Build ranges assume existing approval features can be configured.
unknowns: What are the actual spending limits and contract approval roles?
Can agency proposals be processed under existing confidentiality agreements?
Which campaign fields and procurement interfaces are available?
Are audience inputs aggregated or personally identifiable?
research_questions: Which comparison fields prevent the most consequential scope misunderstandings?
Can the pilot preserve exclusions and usage rights across varied proposal formats?
new_work: Review generated briefs and unresolved questions.
Check extracted exclusions, fees and usage rights against proposals.
Maintain comparison fields and approval thresholds.
Investigate failed transfers between the {PROCUREMENT} and the {PROJECT}.
tasks.statement: Consult with advertising agencies or staff to arrange promotional campaigns in all types of media for products, organizations, or individuals.

tasks.short: Coach representatives to communicate clearly and credibly with the public or employees.

steps.what: Discuss the representative's audience, upcoming communication and development needs.
Prepare practice questions, message examples and a coaching agenda.

loop.input: Coaching brief, approved messages and communication guidelines.
loop.output: Audience-specific questions, hypothetical challenges and source-linked message examples.
loop.check: Check every factual statement against approved material; label hypothetical questions; specialist checks tone and difficulty.
loop.stop: Generate one pack with one revision; unsupported topics return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but realistic questions and examples depend on the audience and situation.

steps.what: Run practice conversations and give specific feedback on delivery and judgement.
Write a personalised practice plan from agreed feedback.

loop.input: Coach-selected notes, agreed goals and approved practice material.
loop.output: Short practice plan with exercises linked to agreed goals.
loop.check: Use only recorded feedback; exclude inferred personality or readiness scores; coach reviews before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; disputed feedback is resolved by the coach and representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning individual feedback into useful exercises requires limited language generation.

steps.what: Arrange the next practice session and send agreed reminders.

tasks.design: Use approved material in the {DOCS} to generate reviewed practice packs and personalised exercises through bounded drafting loops. The coach runs the sessions and agrees development goals, while the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL} handle scheduling and agreed reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coaching itself depends on trust and observation; tailoring preparation and follow-up previously required repeated manual writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-constrained drafting can produce editable practice material, with existing scheduling features handling routine coordination.
tasks.still_hard: A coach must assess anxiety, credibility and situational judgement. Confidential coaching notes require restricted access and careful retention.
tasks.human_edge: Create psychological safety, give candid feedback and recognise when rehearsed language undermines credibility.
tasks.altitude: The coach spends less time writing packs and can support additional novice speakers. Decisions about coaching goals and readiness remain human and within the existing mandate.

reach.task: Prepare a representative for a difficult public interview.
reach.learn: Escalation boundaries, difficult-question practice and evidence-based readiness discussions.

evidence.claim: A trial involving 444 professionals found faster and higher-rated writing with ChatGPT; it did not establish better coaching outcomes.
Acrolinx supports repeatable checks against a style guide, useful for checking practice material.
Personalised practice packs can support human coaching, but readiness and behavioural feedback require contextual judgement.

assumptions: Live coaching remains the largest time component, consistent with the task priors.
The pilot uses coach-selected notes rather than automatic recordings or employee scoring.
Representatives receive only reviewed practice material.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; employee consultation and coaching-data use follow applicable national rules.
Build ranges include access and consultation effort; formal consultation can extend calendar time.
unknowns: Whether representatives are employees, external clients or both.
Who may access coaching notes and how long they are retained.
Which messages and communication guidelines are approved.
Whether first-time supervisors currently receive communication coaching.
research_questions: Which practice questions do coaches find realistic and useful?
Does reduced preparation time allow additional coaching sessions without reducing quality?
new_work: Review generated scenarios for factual accuracy, tone and difficulty.
Remove unsupported or insensitive exercises.
Maintain approved message material and coaching templates.
Review access and retention of personal coaching notes.
tasks.statement: Coach client representatives in effective communication with the public or with employees.

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver speeches that explain the organization's position and build public trust.

steps.what: Discuss the audience, occasion and intended message with the speaker.
Gather approved facts, quotations and earlier statements from the {DOCS}.
Draft the speech and speaker notes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Speech brief, approved source pack and speaker style preferences.
loop.output: Speech draft and notes with source references for claims and exact quotations.
loop.check: Rules validate quotation matches, source identifiers and estimated length; the specialist reviews meaning and voice.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unsupported claims become questions, and invented anecdotes or quotations are rejected.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot produce a coherent spoken narrative suited to the occasion and speaker.

steps.what: Verify technical claims and clear sensitive factual passages.
Revise personal wording and approve the speech script.
Rehearse delivery, timing and likely audience questions with the speaker.
Deliver the speech and respond to the audience.

tasks.design: A deterministic source-pack generator retrieves approved, tagged material from the {DOCS}, then a bounded drafting loop produces a referenced script and speaker notes. Fixed checks catch unmatched quotations and missing references; subject experts and the speaker clear the script, rehearse and deliver it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source material was scattered, and each speaker needed a distinct voice. Earlier automation could format notes but could not draft a useful narrative.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can work from a small approved source pack. Source identifiers, exact quotation checks and existing document versioning constrain the output.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity, emotional timing and live audience response stay human. Source matching cannot establish that a claim remains true or appropriate.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what the speaker can credibly say and adapt to the audience in the room.

ambition.what: Source-backed audience question rehearsal for occasional speakers

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time finding approved material and drafting routine passages, freeing time for rehearsal and audience preparation. The speaker retains responsibility for the words and live delivery.

reach.task: Develop the narrative arc of a speech.
reach.learn: Spoken rhythm, transitions and ethical use of personal stories.

reach.task: Plan speaker timing and audience participation.
reach.learn: Run-of-show planning, accessibility and room constraints.

evidence.claim: A controlled professional-writing study supports potential drafting gains, but does not establish gains in live speech delivery.
Spelling, grammar and style checks are available as existing capabilities.
The digest documents a publishing failure involving invented quotations, supporting exact quotation checks and human review.
Source-pack assembly and speech-specific remaining-time estimates are proposed design assumptions.

assumptions: The task covers a prepared speech with rehearsal; spontaneous speaking would have a different time split.
The speaker may be the specialist or another authorized representative.
Automatic source-pack assembly uses approved tags and registers; it does not discover or validate new facts.
No synthetic voice or likeness is needed.
GDPR applies to personal stories and speaker data. AI transparency obligations should be assessed for the actual publication format.
unknowns: Who usually delivers speeches and who clears sensitive claims?
Does an approved claim and quotation register exist?
Are speeches published, recorded or translated?
Which source material is licensed and permitted for model processing?
research_questions: Can speakers use the generated drafts with fewer structural rewrites?
Do source references remain intact through document revisions and final approval?
new_work: Maintain approved facts, quotations and expiry dates.
Review generated wording for authenticity and unsupported implications.
Recheck factual changes made after expert clearance.

tasks.design: Configure contributor intake in the {WORKFLOW} and keep canonical submissions in the {DOCS}, removing emailed version reconciliation. The {WORKFLOW} releases through the {CMS} or {EMAIL} only when the exact version and destination have approval; later edits invalidate that approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates could format publications, but fragmented submissions and varied prose still required manual assembly and rewriting.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing intake and publishing controls can handle coordination. AI-assisted coding reduces assembly work, while a bounded model can draft from a controlled source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive omissions, financial disclosures, quotation permissions and audience trust require judgement. GDPR applies to employee material; public-interest AI text may require transparency under the EU AI Act.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what matters to readers, challenge misleading framing and protect contributors whose stories carry personal risk.

ambition.what: A plain-language newsletter edition for frontline employees with limited reading time.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting versions and correcting copy to interviewing contributors and assessing audience needs. Release and financial-disclosure decision rights remain with the existing approvers.

reach.task: Build an issue outline around reader questions.
reach.learn: Commissioning, narrative order and evidence-preserving cuts.

reach.task: Prepare accessible publication layouts.
reach.learn: Heading structure, reading order and accessible export checks.

evidence.claim: Configured spelling and grammar checks can handle routine corrections.
Acrolinx supports repeatable house-style scoring and quality gates.
The MIT writing trial included press releases, reports and emails; its gains do not establish whole-task savings here.
Canonical contributor records and version-bound publishing approvals are feasible workflow patterns.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Document work dominates, as the priors suggest; source verification and release judgement remain substantial.
Routine publications have reusable sections and an approved style guide.
Existing model access permits the relevant internal data under GDPR-compliant controls.
Access work includes contributor permissions and employee consultation where national rules require it.
Employee content does not receive a general journalistic exemption from GDPR.

tasks.statement: Prepare or edit organizational publications, such as employee newsletters or stockholders' reports, for internal or external audiences.

tasks.short: Prepare, approve and publish website and social content.

steps.what: Receive the approved brief, copy and assets through the {EMAIL}.
Adapt copy, captions and accessibility descriptions for each channel in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved source copy, supplied assets, channel limits and accessibility guidance.
loop.output: Channel variants, captions and proposed image descriptions.
loop.check: Check length, required links, terms and factual references; a person checks image descriptions and meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per channel across at most five channels; uncertain descriptions return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Formatting rules cannot reliably shorten free text or describe images while preserving meaning; unchanged copy bypasses the loop.

steps.what: Apply templates and attach assets in the {CMS} and {SOCIAL}.
Review previews, claims, asset rights, accessibility, destinations and release timing.
Publish or schedule the approved website content in the {CMS}.
Publish or schedule the approved social posts in the {SOCIAL}.
Check live pages, posts and links against the approved previews.
Copy publication links and dates into the content register in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure content intake, templates, previews and scheduling across the {WORKFLOW}, {CMS} and {SOCIAL}; use a bounded drafting loop only for channel adaptation. Approval binds the content version, assets, destinations and release time, and any edit invalidates it before publication. A deterministic job checks published text and links, flags rendering checks for people, and uses publication receipts as the content register.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel preparation involved repeated copying, separate approval messages and inconsistent publication records. Existing publishing features were often only partly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration handles most staging and scheduling; inexpensive custom checks connect publication receipts, approvals and link validation.
tasks.still_hard: Channel permissions, interface limits, image rights and visual rendering vary. Context-sensitive wording and accessibility descriptions still need review.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a technically correct post is appropriate for the audience and current events.

ambition.what: Accessible channel-ready publication packs for small internal teams.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from uploading and copying links to reviewing content and helping internal teams communicate. Existing publishing authority remains; additional channel rights require explicit delegation.

reach.task: Run a shared editorial calendar and resolve competing publication priorities.
reach.learn: Editorial selection, audience fit and publication sequencing.

reach.task: Improve reusable content templates.
reach.learn: Responsive layout, semantic structure and practical accessibility testing.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides social-post scheduling, supporting configuration before custom publishing code.
Acrolinx provides repeatable house-style checks and quality gates.
Version-bound approvals, publication receipts and link checks can be implemented deterministically.

assumptions: Shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates; today's screen use exceeds the supplied prior for this publishing task.
The {CMS} and {SOCIAL} support drafts, scheduling and appropriate publication access.
The publication gates reuse the preview approval rather than requiring repeated approval.
GDPR and EU AI Act transparency duties are assessed for the content; human review is recorded where relevant.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.

research_questions: Can every target channel preserve approved formatting, links and accessibility descriptions?
Which live-content checks can be automated reliably, and which require visual inspection?
Can publication approval be invalidated immediately when content changes?
new_work: Review channel variants, image descriptions and publication exceptions.
Maintain templates, channel limits and publishing credentials.
Check rights, consent and applicable disclosure requirements.
Handle failed, partial or mistimed publication and approve corrections.

Drafting capacity increases; authority over budgets, sensitive disclosures and public commitments changes only through explicit delegation.
